reason: Recurring pattern: bulk CSV import into a live DB with forced status flags. Lesson: scope the import file to new rows, check collisions first, and handle everyday-word brand aliases via context gates. No existing skill covers seed CSV import.

A bulk import wave from one candidate source produced wrong categories and foreign or discontinued products across hundreds of rows. The skill covers import mechanics and alias collisions but has no post-import audit step. The audit numbers from that run show the scale.

EV seed wave (Oct 2026) exposed gaps: no dry-run step, no near-duplicate check (new slugs duplicated existing zero-opinion entities), bare model names (Air, Seal, J5, G3) and first-name/chemistry brands (Alva, Volta, Smoot) needed alias policy before import, workers needed config deployed before import, and search docs needed rebuild after import. User asked: research products actually sold in Indonesia first, and keep smartphone/charging text from matching EV models.

Episode added EV lines and needed a sub-brand decision and a CSV-only refresh path. Skill lacked both: when a brand row mixes lines, and that CSV-only edits need no deploy but still need matcher cache flush and search rebuild.

Episode fixed 27 live entity names (Iphone->iPhone, Ipad->iPad, Infinix Gt->Infinix GT) that came from slug-derived auto-import. Casing lives in the name column; a live rename reverts on re-import if the CSV row disagrees. Durable import rule.
Folded into entity-catalog-maintenance; detail carried in references/seed-import.md and references/import-scope-evidence.md.
